statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-95837 (GHSA-p7v4-vr35-mj6f, GO-2026-6791): containerd's CRI plugin restored a container from a checkpoint through the CreateContainer API with the process credentials, capabilities, no_new_privs and seccomp state recorded in the checkpoint instead of the security context the orchestrator requested, so a crafted checkpoint image can run with elevated privileges. It affects github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 2.1.0 to before 2.2.7 and 2.3.0 to before 2.3.4; the fix disables restore through CreateContainer by default, in containerd's internal/cri/config and internal/cri/server packages (https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-p7v4-vr35-mj6f, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6791, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/13913 on release/2.3, commit https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/928c03c6898cad95f795300281fdff0dbc55a32f, and https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/13937 on release/2.2). Read the Go build information and the function table (with a reader of the Go symbol table that also works on stripped binaries) of every build-dev package published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: 90 builds, 2.6.4-r0 through the current 2.29.1-r2, each for x86_64 and aarch64 except 2.6.4-r0, which is published for aarch64 only; every download was checked against the index checksum. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times in each index; the repository serves one copy, which matches one of those entries' checksum, and that copy was read. Each package holds one file, the Go program /usr/bin/build. runtime.main is in its function table in every build, so every table was read. The build information of /usr/bin/build lists github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 v2.2.0 to v2.3.7 across the builds, but the vulnerable code is not linked in. In every build, the only containerd packages in any function table are core/remotes/docker, core/remotes/docker/auth, core/remotes/errors, internal/lazyregexp, pkg/identifiers, pkg/reference and version (all under github.com/containerd/containerd/v2), and no Go program in any build contains a function from containerd's internal/cri packages, including internal/cri/server and internal/cri/config. No build lists the older github.com/containerd/containerd module, which the Go advisory also names. A strings search of the oldest and the newest build of the package, on each architecture, also finds no internal/cri package name, which would catch inlined functions. As positive controls, the same function-table read and match find, in containerd v2.3.3 (an affected release) built from source for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, with and without symbol stripping, 399 functions in github.com/containerd/containerd/v2/internal/cri/server, including (*criService).CreateContainer and (*criService).CheckpointContainer, and 21 in internal/cri/config, and the same strings search finds the internal/cri package names there; they also find 519 internal/cri/server functions and 21 internal/cri/config functions in /usr/bin/containerd from the DHI containerd 2.4.2-r5 package (x86_64). The vulnerable code is not present in this package, so the containerd version recorded in its build information does not make it affected.

CVE-2026-95837 (GHSA-p7v4-vr35-mj6f, GO-2026-6791): in containerd 2.1.0 to 2.2.6 and 2.3.0 to 2.3.3, checkpoint restore through the CRI plugin's CreateContainer let CRIU restore the process's credentials, capabilities, no_new_privs and seccomp state from the checkpoint instead of enforcing the requested container configuration. Systems that do not use CRI checkpoint restore are not affected. It is fixed in containerd 2.2.7 and 2.3.4, which disable restore in CreateContainer by default: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-p7v4-vr35-mj6f, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6791, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/13913, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/928c03c6898cad95f795300281fdff0dbc55a32f. Read every package built from the DHI docker source for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository (docker, docker-engine, docker-cli and its other subpackages): 39 builds, 29.4.0-r1 to 29.10.0-r1. docker-cli is published for x86_64 and aarch64 in every build, and so is docker-engine except 29.4.3-r0, which is published for aarch64 only; 29.10.0-r1 is so far published only as docker, docker-cli and docker-engine. The Go programs are /usr/bin/dockerd and /usr/bin/docker-proxy in docker-engine and /usr/bin/docker in docker-cli, each dynamically linked against musl (dockerd in some builds also against libnftables); /usr/bin/docker-init is a link to /sbin/tini-static from another package; the other subpackages hold the dockerd-rootless script, OpenRC and systemd service files, a modules-load.d configuration file, shell completions and documentation, with no ELF, PE or Mach-O files, and the docker package itself installs no files. dockerd embeds containerd client libraries from github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 (v2.2.2 to v2.4.2), but the Go function names (read from each program's function table; dockerd, docker-proxy and docker carry no ELF symbol table before 29.10.0-r1) of every dockerd, docker-proxy and docker program in those builds, on both architectures, include nothing from github.com/containerd/containerd/v2/internal/cri/server or its podsandbox package, the CRI plugin code where CreateContainer and the checkpoint restore live, and no build embeds the older github.com/containerd/containerd module. The same search finds containerd's core/images functions (Dispatch, ChildrenHandler) in every dockerd, and runtime.main in every program. Neither docker-proxy nor docker embeds github.com/containerd/containerd/v2.

CVE-2026-95837: a container restored from an untrusted checkpoint through the containerd CRI CreateContainer API keeps the credentials, capabilities and seccomp state from the checkpoint, bypassing the destination security context. The code is in containerd's CRI plugin (internal/cri/server); containerd 2.2.7 and 2.3.4 disable restore through CreateContainer by default (https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-p7v4-vr35-mj6f, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6791; release/2.3 fix commit https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/928c03c6898cad95f795300281fdff0dbc55a32f, release/2.2 change https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/13937). Read every published trivy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 38 builds, 0.69.1-r0 to the current 0.74.0-r12, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each package checked against the index checksum. Each package installs one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 that keeps its Go symbol table. The Go build information lists github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 2.2.0 to 2.3.3 in builds before 0.74.0-r5 and 2.3.5 to 2.3.7 from 0.74.0-r5 on; builds 0.69.1-r0 to 0.70.0-r6 also list the older github.com/containerd/containerd 1.7 module, which the advisory lists with no fixed version. trivy uses containerd's client and image packages, but the function table of every build (go tool nm) has no function from containerd's CRI packages (internal/cri, pkg/cri or plugins/cri, in either module), while runtime.main is found in each build. A string search of four of the builds (trivy 0.69.1-r0 aarch64 and 0.71.2-r2 x86_64, trivy-dev 0.70.0-r6 aarch64, trivy-fips 0.74.0-r12 x86_64) also finds no containerd CRI package path. As a positive control, the same go tool nm search on /usr/bin/containerd from the DHI containerd 2.4.2-r5 package finds 1663 CRI functions, including internal/cri/server.(*criService).CheckpointContainer. The vulnerable CRI code is not in the shipped binary.
